sections.history: Thiruppathisaram, called Thiruvanparisaram in the hymns, is a village a few kilometres north-east of Nagercoil, and its temple is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham — counted among the shrines of Malai Nadu. Nammalvar sang its lord, and Sri Vaishnava tradition remembers the village with particular tenderness as the home of Udaya Nangai, Nammalvar's mother. The oldest inscription in the temple is dated to 1139 CE and records gifts to the lord, and tradition holds that Thirumalai Nayak of Madurai had a hand in renovating the shrine. Locally the temple is also known as the shrine of Kuralappa Perumal.
sections.architecture: A granite wall encloses the temple and all its shrines, built in the Dravidian manner of the far south. The presiding lord is seated, bearing the conch and the discus, with the Goddess Lakshmi on his chest — the form that gives him his name, 'he of the blessed chest'. Tradition says the image is fashioned not of stone but of a special paste, and so it does not receive ritual bathing (abhishekam). The temple tank, named for Lakshmi, lies opposite the main entrance, outside the walls.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that a king who had lost his horse found it grazing beside the Soma Tirtham here, and there beheld Vishnu; moved by the vision, he built the temple. Tradition identifies this king with the ruler who renounced his throne and became Kulasekhara Alvar, and the temple still keeps the day of his passing to Vaikuntha. The seven sages, the Saptarishis, are also said to have come to this place and sanctified the Soma Tirtham.
sections.festivals: The ten-day Chithirai festival (April–May) is the temple's main celebration. Adi Swati (July–August) recalls the day the lord is said to have taken Kulasekhara Alvar to Vaikuntha; Avani Thiruvonam, the Saturdays of Purattasi and Vaikunta Ekadashi are kept with special worship.
sections.experience: Thiruppathisaram is a quiet village shrine, unhurried and intimate after the bustle of Nagercoil. Pause at the tank before entering, then take darshan of the seated lord with Lakshmi on his chest, and remember Udaya Nangai, Nammalvar's mother, whom tradition links with this village. Pilgrims often combine the visit with Thiruvattar and Thiruvananthapuram on a Malai Nadu journey.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday closure, following the temple's own schedule; festival days are crowded. Confirm current timings locally before you visit.
visit.dressCode: Traditional modest dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered, footwear removed before entering. Follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruppathisaram is a few kilometres north-east of Nagercoil in Kanyakumari district and is reached by road. Nagercoil Junction is the nearest major railway station, and Thiruvananthapuram has the nearest airport.
